label: Look — chromogenic naturalism (large-format colour film)
brief: Large-format colour film, in the spirit of Portra 160 / Ektar 100 sheet film: accurate, well-separated colour, natural shadow falloff, neutral-warm midtones, gentle contrast. It should look photographed, not processed. No HDR shadow lifting, no haze tricks, no edge crunch. Limits (keep within them on every pass): Shadows at most +25; Highlights -15..-45; Dehaze 0; Clarity 0; Texture +5..+15; Saturation and Vibrance small, colour comes from separation, not intensity. Reds a touch warmer and richer, blues slightly deeper and never magenta; a faint warm paper tint in the highlights. Tones (luma 0-255): a real black, p1/p5 about 10-20; open, true middle, p50 about 110-130; bright but unclipped highlights, p95 about 215-230 and p99 under about 240. White balance: neutral-warm; correct a cast, keep the light's character. Masks only where the scene needs them, and gently: a subtle radial or linear to balance a bright sky or a dark foreground, never to sculpt drama. Pass 0 sets the hues; the variant sets its strength (A subtle, B full, C bold). Keep the hues; refine amounts. The user's own request wins wherever it disagrees with this look.
convergence_hints: stop when p50 sits about 110-130, p1 shows a real black and p99 is under about 240 with no high clip
stop when colours are separated and believable: skies blue not magenta, skin and reds warm not orange
do not reach for Dehaze or Clarity: they break this look
